title: Bengaluru's lost lakes: what an old lake bed means for property risk
text:
For anyone buying or lending against property in Bengaluru, what the land was before the city is a risk worth checking.
Greater Bengaluru's lake area fell from 2,342 ha in 1973 to 918 ha in 2007, about 61% (Ramachandra and Kumar 2008, via Citizen Matters). The central bus station itself, Majestic, opened in 1969 on the bed of Dharmambudhi lake.
Built-over lakes and blocked storm-water channels are one reason experts link to the city's recurring floods, which shows up later as waterlogging, insurance and resale questions.
When you assess a site, do you check old maps or lake records, or rely on the approvals alone?
